open_with: Open directly with the concentration finding itself: Kim Do-Yoon currently has 29.7% of total wealth concentrated in North America information technology, spread across just 2 positions and a single instrument type. Frame it analytically as a single-bet exposure question — ask him directly whether this is a deliberate high-conviction thematic stance he wants to press further, or a legacy build-up he hasn't recently stress-tested against a tech-sector drawdown or event-driven shock (rate moves, AI-cycle correction, single-name earnings risk). Given his profile as a sophisticated, aggressive, thematic investor, engage him on the mechanics: two positions, one instrument type means idiosyncratic and structural concentration risk is unusually high even if the sector thesis is sound. Invite him to walk through his conviction level and time horizon on the position before discussing any hedging, collar, or diversification overlay options.
do_not_lead_with: Do not open with generic portfolio review small talk, risk-tolerance disclaimers, or a soft/neutral check-in — there is no restriction or sensitivity flagged on file, nothing blocks this conversation, and he is a direct, analytical investor who will read a hedged opening as either uninformed or patronizing. Also avoid leading with performance/returns commentary before naming the concentration — that buries the actual agenda item and wastes the opening. Don't soften the 29.7% figure or bury it in a broader asset-allocation summary.
